verses.zh: 「我所陈明在你面前的这一切咒诅都临到你身上；你在耶和华―你　神追赶你到的万国中必心里追念祝福的话；
verses.en: “When you have experienced all these things, both the blessings and the curses[NOTE:1] I have set before you, you will reflect upon them[NOTE:2] in all the nations where the Lord your God has banished you.
notes: Heb “the blessing and the curse.”
Heb “and you bring (them) back to your heart.”
verses.commentary:
30:1 "when all of these things have come upon you" Israel's future will be one of two realities based on their
covenant obedience (i.e. Deut. 30:15,19; Psalm 1). YHWH desires "blessings," but their choices will determine which of
the realities (i.e. blessings or cursings, cf. Leviticus 26) comes into being. Human choices are crucial!

▣ "the blessing and the curse" This is known in Wisdom Literature as "the two ways" (Psalm 1). They are described
in Deut. 27; 28; 30:15,19.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING (OT)

▣ "I have set before you" This VERB (BDB 678, KB 723, Qal PERFECT,
cf. Deut. 30:15,19 and note at Deut. 11:26) is imagery for Israel's need to choose one of the two divine consequences
related to His covenant.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION vs. HUMAN FREE WILL

▣ "and you call them to mind" This is an idiom meaning "cause to return to your heart" (BDB 996, KB 1427,
Hiphil PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 4:39; 1 Kgs. 8:47; Isa. 44:19; 46:8).

▣ "in all nations where the Lord your God has banished you" This is predictive
prophecy of the choices Israel would make which would result in exile. Notice YHWH did this because of Israel's continual
covenant violations and imitations of the Canaanite practices.

verses.zh: 你和你的子孙若尽心尽性归向耶和华―你的　神，照着我今日一切所吩咐的听从他的话；
verses.en: Then if you and your descendants[NOTE:1] turn to the Lord your God and obey him with your whole mind and being[NOTE:2] just as[NOTE:3] I am commanding you today,
notes: Heb “sons” (so NASB); KJV, ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT “children.”
Or “heart and soul” (also in vv. 6, 10).
Heb “according to all.”
verses.commentary:
30:2 "return" This same VERB (BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal PERFECT with waw) was
used in Deut. 30:1 (Hiphil PERFECT with waw) in reference to Israel recalling YHWH's covenant. Here it is
used in the sense of repentance. There is hope even for covenant violators!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

30:2-3 This context brings a needed theological balance to the stark judgment of Deut. 29:19. The problem is
not rebellion, but sustained, continual rebellion (i.e. generation after generation). Repentance is always possible from God's side, but humans harden
their own hearts with willful rebellion and disobedience!

For "heart" see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

For "soul" see SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

▣ "Lord" YHWH is the covenant name of God that the rabbis say reflects His
mercy (cf. Gen. 2:4; Exod. 3:13-14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "God" Elohim is the general name for God which conveys power, might and strength (i.e. God as Creator,
Provider, and Sustainer, Genesis 1). The rabbis say it is used of God's justice and righteousness. This distinction between these two
names can be seen in Psalm 103, YHWH, and Psalm 104, Elohim.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣ "obey" Notice that "returns to the Lord" is parallel to "obey Him"
(BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal PERFECT with waw). Obedience is described in personal terms:

- obey his voice ‒ BDB 876 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

- with all your heart ‒ BDB 523

- with all your soul ‒ BDB 659

This is parallel to Deut. 4:29-30; 6:5; 10:12

Notice the number of times and the different senses of the term shub (BDB 996, KB 1427): It is a
key term in this chapter for hope and restoration.

- "call them to mind" is literally "cause them to return to your heart, Deut. 30:1

- "you return to the Lord," Deut. 30:2 (i.e. repentance)

- "God will restore you from captivity," Deut. 30:3

- "again," Deut. 30:3,8,9

- "if you turn to the Lord," Deut. 30:10

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣ "with all your heart and soul" This is an idiom of one's whole being (cf. Deut. 30:2,6,10; 4:29; 6:5; 10:12;
11:13; 13:3; 26:16).

▣ "you and your sons" The ancient covenant is being renewed with the current generation (cf. Deut. 29:1). Israel
was to educate the children as to the historical bases of their faith (cf. Deut. 4:9,10; 6:7,20-25; 11:19; 32:46) so that each new
generation would be part of the ancient covenant.

verses.zh: 那时，耶和华―你的　神必怜恤你，救回你这被掳的子民；耶和华―你的　神要回转过来，从分散你到的万民中将你招聚回来。
verses.en: the Lord your God will reverse your captivity and have pity on you. He will turn and gather you from all the peoples among whom he[NOTE:1] has scattered you.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
verses.commentary:
30:3-4 "God will restore. . .God has scattered" Notice YHWH is in control of history. He uses nations and individuals
but He is sovereign (cf. Isa. 10:5; 44:28-45:1).

30:3-9 Notice what YHWH promised to do for Israel (if they obey, Deut. 30:8,10):

- He will restore (Deut. 30:3, BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal PERFECT with waw)

- He will have compassion (Deut. 30:3, BDB 933, KB 1216, Piel PERFECT with waw)

- He will gather you (BDB 867, KB 1062, Piel PERFECT with waw, twice, Deut. 30:3 and 4)

- He will bring you back (Deut. 30:4, BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERFECT with waw)

- He will bring you into the land (Deut. 30:5, BDB 97, KB 112, Hiphil PERFECT with waw)

- He will prosper you (Deut. 30:5, BDB 405, KB 408, Hiphil PERFECT with waw)

- He will multiply you (Deut. 30:5, BDB 915 I, KB 1176, Hiphil PERFECT with waw)

- He will circumcise your heart (Deut. 30:6, BDB 557 II, KB 555, Qal PERFECT with waw)

- He will inflict all the curses on your enemies (Deut. 30:7, BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PERFECT with waw)

- He will prosper you abundantly (Deut. 30:9, BDB 451, KB 451, Hiphil PERFECT with waw)

- the work of your hand

- the offspring of your body

- the offspring of your cattle

- the produce of your land (the opposite is in Deut. 28:38-42)

- He will again rejoice over you for good (Deut. 30:9, BDB 965, KB 1314 [twice], Qal
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT and Qal PERFECT)

verses.zh: 你被赶散的人，就是在天涯的，耶和华―你的　神也必从那里将你招聚回来。
verses.en: Even if your exiles are in the most distant land,[NOTE:1] from there the Lord your God will gather you and bring you back.
notes: Heb “are at the farthest edge of the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.
verses.commentary:
30:4

NASB
"at the ends of the earth"

NKJV
"to the farthest parts under heaven"

NRSV, JPSOA, REB
"to the ends of the world"

TEV
"to the farthest corners of the earth"

NJB, LXX
"to the very sky's end"

Peshitta
"in the outmost parts of heaven"

This is literally "to the end of the heavens," which is a hyperbole (cf. Deut. 4:32; 28:64;
Jer. 31:8). It refers to the farthest civilizations they knew (i.e. the ANE and Mediterranean cultures).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE CIRCLE OF THE EARTH

verses.zh: 耶和华―你的　神必领你进入你列祖所得的地，使你可以得着；又必善待你，使你的人数比你列祖众多。
verses.en: Then he[NOTE:1] will bring you to the land your ancestors[NOTE:2] possessed and you also will possess it; he will do better for you and multiply you more than he did your ancestors.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on the second occurrence of the word “he” in v. 3.
Heb “fathers” (also later in this verse and in vv. 9, 20).
verses.commentary:
30:5 "which your fathers possessed" This could refer to:

- the Patriarchs (Moses' day)

- the return from the exile (post-exilic editor)

From my study #1 seems best. Verse 9 speaks of the same group.

▣ "He will prosper you and multiply you" This is part of YHWH's promise to Abraham (cf. Genesis 12; 15; 17, etc).

verses.zh: 耶和华―你　神必将你心里和你后裔心里的污秽除掉，好叫你尽心尽性爱耶和华―你的　神，使你可以存活。
verses.en: The Lord your God will also cleanse[NOTE:1] your heart, and the hearts of your descendants[NOTE:2] so that you may love him[NOTE:3] with all your mind and being and so that you may live.
notes: Heb “circumcise” (so KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV); TEV “will give you and your descendents obedient hearts.” See note on the word “cleanse” in Deut 10:16.
Heb “seed” (so KJV, ASV).
Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on the second occurrence of the word “he” in v. 3.
verses.commentary:
30:6 "God will circumcise your heart" This is imagery for an open and accessible hearing of God's word. The
opposite is stated in Deut. 30:17. In Deut. 10:16 and Jer. 4:4; 9:25-26, the Israelite is called upon to perform this spiritual act
(cf. Rom. 2:28-29), yet here God must do it. This same tension between God's sovereignty and human action is seen in
Ezek. 18:31 vs. Ezek. 36:26. Here, circumcision is imagery for a proper spiritual attitude. See full note at Deut. 10:16.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PREDESTINATION (Calvinism) VS. HUMAN FREE WILL (Arminianism)

▣ "heart" For the Hebrews this was the center of intellectual activity.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

▣ "descendants" This is literally "seed" (BDB 282). This term is used in this figurative sense
several times in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 1:8; 4:37; 10:15; 11:9; 28:46,59; 30:6,19; 31:21; 34:4).

▣ "soul" This is the Hebrew word nephesh (BDB659). See notes at Deut. 11:13 and Gen. 35:18; Lev. 17:11 online.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

verses.zh: 耶和华―你的　神必将这一切咒诅加在你仇敌和恨恶你、逼迫你的人身上。
verses.en: Then the Lord your God will put all these curses on your enemies, on those who hate you and persecute you.

verses.zh: 你必归回，听从耶和华的话，遵行他的一切诫命，就是我今日所吩咐你的。
verses.en: You will return and obey the Lord, keeping all his commandments I am giving[NOTE:1] you today.
notes: Heb “commanding”; NAB “which I now enjoin on you.”
verses.commentary:
30:8-9 This reflects what YHWH wanted to do for Israel and for the whole world!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 你若听从耶和华―你　神的话，谨守这律法书上所写的诫命律例，又尽心尽性归向耶和华―你的　神，他必使你手里所办的一切事，并你身所生的，牲畜所下的，地土所产的，都绰绰有余；因为耶和华必再喜悦你，降福与你，像从前喜悦你列祖一样。
verses.en: The Lord your God will make the labor of your hands[NOTE:1] abundantly successful and multiply your children,[NOTE:2] the offspring of your cattle, and the produce of your soil. For the Lord will once more[NOTE:3] rejoice over you to make you prosperous[NOTE:4] just as he rejoiced over your ancestors,
notes: The MT reads “hand” (singular). Most versions read the plural.
Heb “the fruit of your womb” (so NAB, NIV); NRSV “of your body.”
Heb “return and.” The Hebrew verb is used idiomatically here to indicate the repetition of the following action.
The Hebrew text includes “for good.”

verses.zh: a
verses.en: if you obey the Lord your God and keep his commandments and statutes that are written in this scroll of the law. But you must turn to him[NOTE:1] with your whole mind and being.
notes: Heb “to the Lord your God.” See note on the second occurrence of the word “he” in v. 3.
verses.commentary:
30:10 "if. . .if" This shows the conditional nature of the covenant. Notice that obedience (listen and keep) are
paralleled with sincere and total commitment (with all your heart and soul).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

verses.zh: 「我今日所吩咐你的诫命不是你难行的，也不是离你远的；
verses.en: “This commandment I am giving[NOTE:1] you today is not too difficult for you, nor is it too remote.
notes: Heb “commanding”; NAB “which I enjoin on you.”
verses.commentary:
30:11-14 YHWH's will for Israel was not impossible (cf. Deut. 28:29). This verse seems to depreciate the
reformers doctrine of "total depravity." There are several places in the OT where human resistence to sin is
possible (e.g. Gen. 4:7; Deut. 30:15,19).

The church (i.e. Paul) picks up on Genesis 3 as the origin of sin in mankind, while Rabbinical Midrash picks up on
Genesis 6 as the source of the conflict. As Christianity asserts the fallenness of all creation (i.e. Rom. 8:18-19), including humanity (Rom. 3:23),
Judaism asserts the basic goodness of humanity. For them the evil is in the choice (i.e. yetzer), not the basic nature.

However, it seems to me that moral accountability is based on the real possibility of comprehending
God's will and the ability to act on it. Without the possibility of appropriate action, divine accountability is inappropriate! Can
I be held responsible for that which I cannot do?

verses.zh: 不是在天上，使你说：『谁替我们上天取下来，使我们听见可以遵行呢？』
verses.en: It is not in heaven, as though one must say, ‘Who will go up to heaven to get it for us and proclaim it to us so we may obey it?’
verses.commentary:
30:12 "'Who will go up to heaven'" Paul uses this in Rom. 10:6-9. It possibly reflects the Sumerian legend of
Etana, but probably relates to the Hebrew view of God's sovereignty.

There are several VERBS used in an imperatival sense in this verse (according to
OT Parsing Guide):

- "to get it" ‒ BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERFECT, but JUSSIVE in meaning

- "make us hear" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Hiphil IMPERFECT, but JUSSIVE in meaning

- "we may observe it" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERFECT, but COHORTATIVE in meaning

verses.zh: 也不是在海外，使你说：『谁替我们过海取了来，使我们听见可以遵行呢？』
verses.en: And it is not across the sea, as though one must say, ‘Who will cross over to the other side of the sea and get it for us and proclaim it to us so we may obey it?’
verses.commentary:
30:13 "beyond the sea" Some see this as related to the Babylonian flood account called the Gilgamesh Epic, but
it probably relates to the Jewish fears of sailing or imagery of the ends of the earth.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE CREATION ACCOUNTS AND FLOOD TEXTS

verses.zh: 这话却离你甚近，就在你口中，在你心里，使你可以遵行。
verses.en: For the thing is very near you—it is in your mouth and in your mind[NOTE:1] so that you can do it.
notes: Heb “heart.”
verses.commentary:
30:14 "But the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart" This refers to YHWH's revealed covenant. The
ancients read Scripture aloud! They had to appropriately respond inwardly to what they had heard (i.e. read themselves or
read aloud).

▣ "that you may observe it" Humans must make the decision. It is in his ability to do so. God initiates but
mankind must respond and continue to respond in repentance, faith, obedience, worship, and perseverance! This is the nature of "covenant."

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 「看哪，我今日将生与福，死与祸，陈明在你面前。
verses.en: “Look! I have set before you today life and prosperity on the one hand, and death and disaster on the other.
verses.commentary:
30:15 "See" This (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERATIVE) VERB is used as an
idiom for "pay close attention to" (cf. Gen. 27:27; 31:50). It is used several times in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 1:8,21,35; 2:24,31;
4:5; 11:26; 30:15; 32:39.

▣ "I have set before you today life and prosperity, and death and adversity" Even covenant Israel had to
choose (i.e. conditional covenant)! This is referring to covenant blessing and cursing (cf. Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-28).

Remember, the choice is set in a covenant of grace. This is very similar to Wisdom Literature's idiom of the "two ways"
(cf. Psalm 1; Prov. 4:10-19; Jer. 21:8; Matt. 7:13-14). Our choices show who we are! How we respond to life's inexplicable "in and outs" reveals
our spiritual orientation! Eternal life has observable characteristics!

verses.zh: 吩咐你爱耶和华―你的　神，遵行他的道，谨守他的诫命、律例、典章，使你可以存活，人数增多，耶和华―你　神就必在你所要进去得为业的地上赐福与你。
verses.en: What[NOTE:1] I am commanding you today is to love the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, and to obey his commandments, his statutes, and his ordinances. Then you will live and become numerous and the Lord your God will bless you in the land that you are about to possess.[NOTE:2]
notes: A number of LXX mss insert before this verse, “if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God,” thus translating אֲשֶׁר (ʾasher) as “which” and the rest as “I am commanding you today, to love,” etc., “then you will live,” etc.
Heb “which you are going there to possess it.” This has been simplified in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
30:16-18 These verses are a summary of covenant conditions and consequences:

- the responsibility (cf. Deut. 8:6; 19:9; 26:17; 28:9)

- "to love the Lord," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 12, KB 17, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)

- "walk in His ways," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 229, KB 246, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)

- "keep His commandments," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal INFINITIVE; see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

- the consequences of obedience

- "you may live," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 310, KB 309, Qal PERFECT with waw)

- "you may multiply," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 915, KB 1156, Qal PERFECT with waw)

- "your God may bless you," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 138, KB 159, Piel PERFECT with waw)

- the conditions and consequences of disobedience

- if your heart turns away," Deut. 30:17 (BDB 815, KB 937, Qal IMPERFECT with waw)

- "if you will not obey," Deut. 30:17; (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT with waw)

- idolatry

(1) drawn away (BDB 623, KB 673, Niphil PERFECT with waw)

(2) worship (BDB 1005, KB 295, Hishtaphel PERFECT with waw)

(3) serve (BDB 712, KB 773, Qal PERFECT with waw; see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)

- "you shall surely perish," Deut. 30:18 (BDB 1, KB 2, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
and Qal IMPERFECT of the same root, which expresses intensity)

- "you shall not prolong your days," Deut. 30:18 (BDB 73, KB 88, Hiphil IMPERFECT)

Notice how Deut. 30:20 reinforces these covenant responsibilities so that the Patriarchal blessing can
be fulfilled! This terminology is characteristic of Deuteronomy.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEGREES OF REWARDS AND PUNISHMENT

verses.zh: 倘若你心里偏离，不肯听从，却被勾引去敬拜事奉别神，
verses.en: However, if you[NOTE:1] turn aside and do not obey, but are lured away to worship and serve other gods,
notes: Heb “your heart,” as a metonymy for the person.

verses.zh: 我今日明明告诉你们，你们必要灭亡；在你过约旦河、进去得为业的地上，你的日子必不长久。
verses.en: I declare to you this very day that you[NOTE:1] will certainly[NOTE:2] perish! You will not extend your time in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess.[NOTE:3]
notes: To this point in the chapter, Moses has addressed the people with the singular pronoun “you,” but here he switches to the plural. Rhetorically, the singular pronoun has emphasized the responsibilities and consequences for the nation as a whole. It is a group responsibility that requires a group effort. At v. 18 he shifts to using the plural form. This individualizes the threatened punishment in v. 18 and highlights individual responsibility in the first half of v. 19 (calling heaven and earth as witness “against you”) before returning to the collective responsibility that “you” (singular) choose life.
The Hebrew text uses the infinitive absolute for emphasis, which the translation indicates with “certainly.”
Heb “to go there to possess it.”

verses.zh: 我今日呼天唤地向你作见证；我将生死祸福陈明在你面前，所以你要拣选生命，使你和你的后裔都得存活；
verses.en: Today I invoke heaven and earth as witnesses against you that I have set life and death, blessing and curse, before you. Therefore choose life so that you and your descendants may live!
verses.commentary:
30:19 "I call heaven and earth to witness" These witnesses were not unique to Israel's covenant, but are found
in several ANE texts. These two permanent aspects of God's creation (cf. Gen. 1:1) function as God's two required witnesses
(cf. Deut. 17:6; 19:15; Num. 35:30). This legal emphasis occurs several times in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:26; 30:19; 31:28; 32:1).

For "Earth" see SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH.

▣ "So choose life in order that you may live" God has given humans the right and responsibility to
make moral choices. It is part of His image and likeness in mankind (i.e. Gen.1:26-27)! The Hebrew VERB, "to choose"
or "to elect," is used 70% of the time for mankind's choice (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 639). We must choose (cf. Ezek. 18:30-32)!

▣ "you and your descendants" Deuteronomy characteristically emphasizes the need to pass on the
covenant history and responsibilities to the succeeding generations (cf. Deut. 4:9,10; 6:7,20-25; 11:19; 32:46).

Our children are affected by our lifestyle choices and instruction (cf. Exod. 20:5-6; Deut. 5:9-10; 7:9).

verses.zh: 且爱耶和华―你的　神，听从他的话，专靠他；因为他是你的生命，你的日子长久也在乎他。这样，你就可以在耶和华向你列祖亚伯拉罕、以撒、雅各起誓应许所赐的地上居住。」
verses.en: I also call on you[NOTE:1] to love the Lord your God, to obey him and be loyal to him, for he gives you life and enables you to live continually[NOTE:2] in the land the Lord promised to give to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
notes: The words “I also call on you” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. In the Hebrew text vv. 19-20 are one long sentence, which the translation divides into two.
Heb “he is your life and the length of your days to live.”
verses.commentary:
30:20 There is a series of Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS which summarize the covenant:

- responsibilities

- loving

- obeying

- holding fast

- consequences ‒ that you may dwell in the land

See note at Deut. 30:16-18. YHWH's covenant demanded an initial and a continual faith, love, obedience, and perseverance.

YHWH promised the land to Israel's patriarchs (cf. Gen. 12:7; 13:14-17; Deut. 9:4-6), but Israel must obey
His covenant requirements or the land would be forfeited (cf. Deut. 11:31-32; 28:36,63-68; 30:19-20). The grace gift (unconditional covenant) must
be responded to and maintained (conditional covenant)!

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.
